title: Chapter 1: Propositional Logic and Set Theory
content:
ሰላም የEthioFresh ቤተሰቦች! 👋 እንኳን ወደ Mathematics ትምህርት በሰላም መጣችሁ። ይህ ኖት ሞጁሉን ሙሉ በሙሉ በዝርዝር የሚያብራራ፣ ሌላ ማጣቀሻ እንዳያስፈልጋችሁ ተደርጎ የተዘጋጀ ነው። ደብተራችሁን አውጡ፣ ትኩረታችሁን ሰብሰብ አድርጉ... እንጀምር! 🚀

1.1. Propositional Logic
Mathematical or symbolic logic is an analytical theory of the art of reasoning whose goal is to systematize and codify principles of valid reasoning.

1.1.1 Definition and Examples of Propositions

Definition 1.1: A proposition (or statement) is a sentence which has a truth value (either True or False but not both). Propositions are usually denoted by letters such as p, q, r, s.

👉 እውነት (True) ወይም ውሸት (False) ተብሎ በግልፅ ሊፈረጅ የሚችል አረፍተ ነገር።

💡 Important Tips / Solution Strategies:
• ጥያቄዎች (Questions)፣ ትዕዛዞች (Commands)፣ እና አጋኖዎች (Exclamations) ፕሮፖዚሽን ሊሆኑ አይችሉም ምክንያቱም እውነት ወይም ውሸት ተብለው አይመለሱም።
• ዋጋቸው ያልታወቁ ፊደላትን የያዙ አረፍተ ነገሮች (ለምሳሌ x + 5 = 10) ፕሮፖዚሽን አይደሉም። ነገር ግን x የተወሰነ ቁጥር ከተሰጠው ፕሮፖዚሽን ይሆናል።
• የአንድን አረፍተ ነገር እውነትነት አሁን ላይ ባናውቀውም እንኳን (ለምሳሌ ታሪካዊ መረጃ በማምጣት)፣ አረፍተ ነገሩ በተፈጥሮው እውነት ወይም ውሸት የመሆን ባህሪ ካለው ፕሮፖዚሽን ነው።

Worked Examples:
Consider the following sentences from the module:
• Example 1: 2 is an even number.
Step 1: It is a declarative sentence.
Step 2: Its truth value is True. Therefore, it is a Proposition.
• Example 2: A triangle has four sides.
Step 1: It is a declarative sentence.
Step 2: Its truth value is False. Therefore, it is a Proposition.
• Example 3: Athlete Haile G/silassie weighed 45 kg when he was 20 years old.
Step 1: Although we might not have the historical record at hand, the statement is inherently either true or false.
Step 2: It cannot be both. Therefore, it is a Proposition.
• Example 4: May God bless you!
Step 1: This is an exclamation/wish.
Step 2: It has no truth value. Therefore, it is Not a proposition.
• Example 5: Give me that book.
Step 1: This is a command.
Step 2: It cannot be asserted or denied. Therefore, it is Not a proposition.
• Example 6: What is your name?
Step 1: This is a question.
Step 2: It has no truth value. Therefore, it is Not a proposition.


1.1.2 Logical Connectives

1. Conjunction (∧ - "and")
The conjunction of two propositions p and q is the proposition p ∧ q. It is True if and only if both p and q are True.

👉 ሁለቱም True ሲሆኑ ብቻ True የሚሆንበት አያያዥ።

pqp ∧ q
TTT
TFF
FTF
FFF


Worked Examples: Let p: "3 is an odd number" (T) and q: "27 is a prime number" (F).
• p ∧ q: "3 is an odd number and 27 is a prime number." Truth value is False (since q is F).


2. Disjunction (∨ - "or")
The disjunction of two propositions p and q is the proposition p ∨ q. It is False if and only if both p and q are False.

👉 ሁለቱም False ሲሆኑ ብቻ False የሚሆንበት አያያዥ። (ቢያንስ አንዱ True ከሆነ True ይሆናል)።

pqp ∨ q
TTT
TFT
FTT
FFF


💡 Solution Strategies:
• በሒሳብ ውስጥ "or" የሚባለው Inclusive or ነው። ይህም ማለት "p ወይም q ወይም ሁለቱም" ማለት ነው።

Worked Examples: Let p: "3 is an odd number" (T) and q: "27 is a prime number" (F).
• p ∨ q: "3 is an odd number or 27 is a prime number." Truth value is True (since p is T).


3. Implication (⇒ - "If..., then...")
The implication p ⇒ q is False if and only if p is True and q is False. (p is called the hypothesis, q is the conclusion).

👉 መነሻው (p) True ሆኖ መድረሻው (q) False ሲሆን ብቻ False የሚሆን ጥብቅ ህግ።

pqp ⇒ q
TTT
TFF
FTT
FFT


💡 Important Tips:
ፈተና ላይ p ⇒ q በተለያዩ መንገዶች ሊፃፍ ይችላል። የሚከተሉትን በደንብ መያዝ ግድ ይላል፡
• If p, then q.
• q if p.
• p implies q.
• p only if q.
• p is sufficient for q.
• q is necessary for p.

Worked Examples: Let p: "3 is an odd number" (T) and q: "27 is a prime number" (F).
• p ⇒ q: "If 3 is an odd number, then 27 is a prime number." Truth value is False (T ⇒ F is F).


4. Bi-implication (⇔ - "if and only if")
The bi-implication p ⇔ q is True if and only if p and q have the same truth values.

👉 ሁለቱም ተመሳሳይ ሲሆኑ (T እና T, ወይም F እና F) ብቻ True የሚሰጥ።

pqp ⇔ q
TTT
TFF
FTF
FFT


💡 Important Tips / Solution Strategies:
ይህም በተለያዩ ቃላት ሊገለፅ ይችላል፡
• p if and only if q (ወይም p iff q).
• p implies q and q implies p.
• p is necessary and sufficient for q.

Worked Examples: Let p: "3 is an odd number" (T) and q: "27 is a prime number" (F).
• p ⇔ q: "3 is an odd number if and only if 27 is a prime number." Truth value is False.


5. Negation (¬ - "not")
The negation of a proposition p is ¬p. It has the opposite truth value of p.

👉 ያለውን ሃሳብ ሙሉ በሙሉ መገልበጥ (True ከሆነ False፣ False ከሆነ True ማድረግ)።

p¬p
TF
FT


Worked Examples:
• Let p: "Addis Ababa is the capital city of Ethiopia." (T).
¬p: "Addis Ababa is not the capital city of Ethiopia." Truth value is False.

😂 የሎጂክ ቀልድ: ሎጂክ ክላስ ላይ ጓደኛህ 'ካጠናሁ A አገኛለሁ' ብሎ (p ⇒ q)፣ ሳያጠና ቀርቶ A ቢያመጣ 'ውሸታም!' አትበለው... ምክንያቱም በ Implication ህግ p (ማጥናቱ) False ከሆነ አረፍተነገሩ በሙሉ True ነው! 😜


1.1.3 Compound Propositions and Logical Equivalences

Definition 1.2: A proposition formed by joining two or more propositions is a compound proposition. (Example: p ∧ (q ∨ r)).

Precedence (ቅደም ተከተል): ቅንፍ ከሌለ በመጀመሪያ ¬, ቀጥሎ ∧ ወይም ∨, በመጨረሻም ⇒ ወይም ⇔ ይሰራል፡፡

Definition 1.3: Two compound propositions P and Q are logically equivalent (written as P ≡ Q) if they have the exact same truth values for all possible combinations.

👉 በቴብል ላይ ሙሉ በሙሉ ተመሳሳይ ውጤት ካላቸው Equivalent (≡) ይባላሉ።

Conditional Statements (ለ p ⇒ q):
1. Converse: q ⇒ p (ቦታ መቀየር)
2. Inverse: ¬p ⇒ ¬q (ባሉበት መካድ)
3. Contrapositive: ¬q ⇒ ¬p (ቦታ ቀይሮ መካድ)

💡 Important Tips:
• ፈተና ላይ የማይቀር ወርቃማ ህግ: አንድ Implication ሁልጊዜም ከ Contrapositive ጋር Equivalent ነው! (p ⇒ q ≡ ¬q ⇒ ¬p). ነገር ግን ከ Converse ወይም Inverse ጋር አቻ አይደለም።

Worked Examples:
• Example: Write the converse, inverse, and contrapositive of "If Kidist lives in Addis Ababa, then she lives in Ethiopia." (p ⇒ q)
Step 1 (Converse - q ⇒ p): If Kidist lives in Ethiopia, then she lives in Addis Ababa.
Step 2 (Inverse - ¬p ⇒ ¬q): If Kidist does not live in Addis Ababa, then she does not live in Ethiopia.
Step 3 (Contrapositive - ¬q ⇒ ¬p): If Kidist does not live in Ethiopia, then she does not live in Addis Ababa.

Important Logical Equivalences to Memorize:
• De Morgan's Laws:
1. ¬(p ∧ q) ≡ ¬p ∨ ¬q
2. ¬(p ∨ q) ≡ ¬p ∧ ¬q
• Distributive Laws:
1. p ∨ (q ∧ r) ≡ (p ∨ q) ∧ (p ∨ r)
2. p ∧ (q ∨ r) ≡ (p ∧ q) ∨ (p ∧ r)
• Complement Law: ¬(¬p) ≡ p


1.1.4 Tautology and Contradiction

Definition:
• Tautology: A compound proposition that is always True regardless of the truth values of its components. (Example: p ∨ ¬p)
• Contradiction: A compound proposition that is always False. (Example: p ∧ ¬p)
• Contingency: A proposition that is neither a tautology nor a contradiction.

👉 ቴብሉ ሙሉ በሙሉ T ከተሞላ Tautology፣ ሙሉ በሙሉ F ከተሞላ Contradiction ይባላል።

Worked Examples:
• Example: Determine if p ∨ ¬p is a tautology.
Step 1: If p is T, ¬p is F. (T ∨ F) = True.
Step 2: If p is F, ¬p is T. (F ∨ T) = True.
Conclusion: Since it is always True, it is a Tautology.


Practice Questions

ከሞጁሉ የተወሰዱ ወሳኝ ጥያቄዎች (እስኪ እራሳችሁን ፈትኑ!)

1. Let p and q be statements. Which of the following implies that p ∨ q is False? (Hint: Think about when "or" becomes false).
a) ¬p ∨ ¬q is false.
b) ¬p ∧ ¬q is true.
c) p ⇒ q is true.

2. Suppose the truth value of p ⇒ q is T. What can be said about the value of ¬p ∧ q ⇔ p ∨ q? (This is a trick question from the module, try substituting different values for p and q that make p⇒q true!).

3. Construct the truth table for each of the following statements and determine if they are tautology, contradiction, or contingency:
a) p ⇒ (p ⇒ q)
b) (p ∧ q) ⇒ (p ∨ s)

4. Write the contrapositive and the converse of: "If it rains, Tigist does not take a walk."

5. [EthioFresh Trick Question]: If (p ∧ q) ⇒ r is False, what are the exact truth values of p, q, and r?
